title: Therapy & Support — choose the composition
question: Same world as Home and About (paper, stone, wine, Inter, black pill). The choice here is how the page is arranged. Lock one.

options.label: Place Yourself, Then Read
options.lineage: Home's "Who I work with" row list, raised to page scale
options.thesis: One screen to find your own row, then three chapters long enough to actually answer you.
options.viewport: Page title and the opening paragraph on the left; beneath it a three-row index — Parents, Teens, Adults — set at heading scale with one line each, Parents first and deepest. The Parents chapter begins before the fold ends.
options.risk: The index repeats what Home already says; if it is set timidly it reads as a second navigation bar rather than a triage.

options.label: The Focal Rail
options.lineage: the anveril.com capture saved to this project's Hub board
options.thesis: One photograph holds the page; a three-name rail beside it changes whose story you are reading.
materials: one tall photograph at real scale
options.viewport: Title and opening paragraph across the top; below, a quiet rail of three names on the left, a single tall photograph in the middle, and the chosen audience's copy on the right. Parents is open on arrival.
options.risk: Two thirds of the page's substance is hidden behind a control, and the long Parents copy has to fit a column that Teens and Adults will underfill.

options.label: Said Out Loud
options.lineage: the `statement` register already carried on About's wine band
options.thesis: Every chapter opens on a sentence the visitor has already thought, and then answers it.
materials: wine statement at display scale opening each chapter
photographs only where a chapter earns one
options.viewport: Page title, the opening paragraph, then immediately the first recognition set large in wine — "How do I stop this behavior?" — with the Parents chapter answering it directly underneath.
options.risk: Three statements in a row becomes a rhythm the reader learns to skip, and the wine loses its force by the third one.
